Tesla Is Running Their Old Announce And Delay Playbook With The Roadster
Tesla keeps setting bold product deadlines, and the stock keeps rallying on the reveal before the date quietly disappears. With several major 2026 targets now on the clock, investors face a question of whether this time is different or the…
Published September 30, 2026, 7:15am ET · 3 min read
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
A Tesla Roadster is displayed in front of a large screen showcasing the Tesla Motors logo, embodying the company's ambitious product visions often met with significant delays. © Introducing the Tesla (CC BY 2.0) by Steve Jurvetson
Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA | TSLA Price Prediction) trades at $352.84, and the setup looks poor. The long-delayed Roadster shows a pattern: Tesla announces products faster than it ships them. Shares are down 21.54% this year as the market prices in that credibility gap.
Tesla revealed the next-generation Roadster in 2017 and promised deliveries by 2020. Its latest annual filing still lists the car as “in design development” with no timeline. Cybertruck was promised for 2021 and arrived in late 2023. The Semi, also unveiled in 2017, is still listed as starting production in 2026.
Record Deliveries and a $43.5 Billion Cash Pile Power the Robotaxi Pitch
Second-quarter revenue rose 25.5% to $28.24 billion, beating estimates. Record deliveries reached 480,126 vehicles. Energy storage installations grew 41% to 13.5 GWh. FSD (Tesla’s paid driver-assistance software) rose to 1.48 million active subscriptions.
Robotaxi operates in seven U.S. markets after logging “more than 380,000 miles of unsupervised Robotaxi” with “zero notable incidents.” FSD also won approval in Croatia. With $43.5 billion in cash, Tesla can fund its AI ambitions for years.
A 344x Earnings Multiple Sits on Shrinking Profits
Tesla is priced at 344 times trailing earnings and 159 times forward earnings. Second-quarter EPS of $0.33 missed expectations of $0.54. Operating margin fell to 1.4%, and free cash flow came in at negative $1.09 billion.
Management expects 2026 capex above $25 billion and is lining up debt facilities of up to $30 billion. Energy gross margin dropped from 39.5% to 20.4%.
Optimus and Cybercab Deadlines Decide Whether Patience Pays
Tesla finished the quarter with its largest order backlog since 2023. The CEO described Optimus as “the hardest product to scale manufacturing that we’ve ever made at Tesla,” with an early ramp that will be “quite flat and long.” Whether Cybercab, Semi, and Megapack 3 reach volume production in 2026 as planned will determine which side wins.
Wall Street Sees Upside While Tesla Lags the Market Badly
The 46 analysts covering Tesla have an average target of $395.83, indicating 12.2% upside. Ratings break down as follows:
Over the past year, Tesla fell 20.39% while the S&P 500 gained 15.16%. The stock also trades below its 200-day moving average of $395.18.
Credibility Gap Weighs on Tesla Until Deadlines Turn Into Deliveries
The risk/reward looks poor at $352.84.
Tesla announces products with firm dates, the stock rallies on the reveal, and the deadline slips out of sight. The Roadster is the clearest case. Hype moves the price while promises keep falling through.
The biggest risk comes over the next few quarters. Tesla has several 2026 production targets due and capex that keeps growing. If Cybercab or Semi volumes slip into next year while margins stay near 1.4%, the multiple has room to compress. Operating expenses are also expected to keep growing.
Two things would force a rethink: free cash flow turning positive again and Semi shipping in real volume on schedule. Until either happens, watch the stock but stay skeptical of each new reveal.
At $352.84, Tesla’s valuation appears to price in more credibility than its delivery record has earned.

The robotaxi industry has moved from an experimental concept toward a potentially massive transportation market. Goldman Sachs Research estimates that the global robotaxi market could reach roughly $415 billion by 2035, with the United States accounting for about $48 billion. That opportunity has put two names at the center of the race— Tesla TSLA and Alphabet's GOOGL Waymo.
Both are pursuing autonomous mobility, but their strategies are fundamentally different. Waymo has built an early lead through real-world deployments, while Tesla is betting that a simpler technology stack and its manufacturing scale can eventually change the economics of the business.
While Alphabet carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), Tesla holds a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) currently.

That scale matters for more than just revenues. Every additional ride gives Waymo more opportunity to familiarize consumers with driverless transportation and build confidence in the technology. Waymo is not just expanding its network, it is helping create the market Tesla eventually wants to compete in.
Waymo's lead, however, comes with a substantial cost. The company continues to invest heavily in technology and geographic expansion and remains unprofitable. Its capital-intensive model means that scaling the business requires significant investment.
Tesla entered the commercial robotaxi race later, launching its service in Austin in June 2025. facts.text: Tesla is showcasing its Cybercab robotaxi at the Paris Motor Show from October 12-18, 2026, with no steering wheel or pedals.
Tesla's Cybercab robotaxi has no manual override controls and faces regulatory challenges in Europe.
Waymo provides over 500,000 fully autonomous paid rides weekly across 15 major U.S. cities.
Tesla's stock rose approximately 0.6% on the day of the Paris Motor Show announcement and gained about 7% over the prior week.
Goldman Sachs Research estimates the global robotaxi market could reach $415 billion by 2035, with the U.S. accounting for $48 billion.
Waymo provides more than 500,000 fully autonomous paid rides each week across 15 major U.S. cities.
Tesla stock rose about 2% in early Tuesday trading, extending a three-day rally that added roughly 8% to shares.
SpaceX stock jumped 17% over a three-day stretch, with gains for a third straight session.
Tesla and SpaceX are in early talks with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing about building a dedicated chip facility (Terafab).
Analysts expect Tesla to report earnings on Oct 21 with EPS of 44 cents per share, down from 50 cents a year ago.
Musk's 42% stake in SpaceX is worth close to $1 trillion at current prices.
HSBC raised its price target but kept a Reduce rating on Tesla, citing Tesla's price-to-earnings ratio above 350.
Tesla's average analyst rating is Hold with a price target near $412.
Tesla ships 'spooky' Halloween Mode with creepy and fun features including Trick or Treat sounds, ghost visualization, and remote voice communication.
Tesla announced AC bidirectional charging for new Model 3 and Model Y with Powerwall 3, extending home backup by two days (vs. one day for Cybertruck).
Tesla Model 3 and Model Y now support Powershare Home Backup with Powerwall 3, extending home backup by over two days during outages for vehicles ordered since October 1, 2026.
Powershare Home Backup requires Powerwall 3 and is limited to vehicles ordered in the US and Puerto Rico after October 1, 2026.
Tesla previously delayed Powershare Home Backup for Model 3 and Model Y, with Cybertruck being the only Tesla model capable of it until this update.
Model 3 and Model Y add up to two days of backup for homes using 30 kWh/day, starting from a 90% charge.
Tesla's Powershare feature for Model 3 and Model Y uses PCS2 Lite inverter technology, requiring hardware updates for specific trims.
Tesla missed its 2025 deadline for Powershare Home Backup, which was previously targeted for release within two years of March 2023 Investor Day.
Ford and GM have already implemented vehicle-to-home capabilities in their EVs, with GM offering it across Ultium-based EVs by 2026.
Goldman Sachs maintains a $360 price target for Tesla stock, below current level of $378.73, with a Neutral rating from analyst Mark Delaney.
Tesla's AI initiatives, including robotaxis, Full Self-Driving, humanoid robots, and custom AI inference chips, are expected to be more significant for the stock than Q3 earnings.
Tesla sold 486,532 vehicles in Q3, exceeding forecasts.
Baird, RBC Capital Markets, Ladenburg Thalmann, and Deutsche Bank have price targets of $475, $480, $475, and $420 respectively for Tesla stock.
HSBC has a $157 target with a 'Reduce' rating for Tesla stock.
Goldman Sachs reiterated a 'Neutral' rating and $360 price target for TSLA, implying ~6% downside from current levels.
Croatia approved FSD (Supervised) EU-wide vote for FSD approval expected in December.
TSLA shares up ~1% at time of writing, with 28% gain since July low of $297.38.
Tesla showcased Cybercab robotaxi at Paris Motor Show starting Oct. 12
Tesla has $6.2 billion in free cash flow and very little debt on its balance sheet.

Tesla launched Halloween Mode with creepy and spooky features for its vehicles.
XLK's annual return was 41.07% through October 5, 2026.
Tesla's base case model shows a $10,000 investment could be worth $13,938 by 2030 at $464.44 per share.
Wall Street's consensus target for Tesla is $396.62, with 6 strong buys, 16 buys, 19 holds, 3 sells, and 2 strong sells.
Tesla's stock trades at 372x trailing earnings and 174x forward earnings with a beta of 1.85.
